data.name: Daemonsgate
data.detailed_description:
Do you feel the darkness approaching?
A mysterious and calamitous scourge of daemons has risen from the southern mountains, devastating the lands of Elsopea and vanishing its populations. Now, the great city of Tormis is under siege! Captain Gustavus, a loyal agent of the king of Tormis, must set out on a quest over land and sea to find a rumored sage who may hold key secrets to uncover the sinister cause of the daemon invasion and bring it to an end!

Experience Imagitec Design’s ambitious and innovative RPG, breathtaking in scope at over 150 hours of play time. Daemonsgate will draw you in with its richly detailed world, fascinating character interactions, and epic story.

  • Explore a vast land beautifully illustrated through more than 3,000 travel screens.
  • Interact with and discover the personalities of Hestor’s many inhabitants using a conversation system with an impressive dictionary of over 70,000 words.
  • Recruit allies and harness their abilities, skills, and three kinds of magic to fight against hordes of enemies.
  • Immerse yourself in the epic and atmospheric soundtrack.

reviews.review:
I played this game "A Lot" when it first came out, so it can't be that bad ... however it does have it's faults the largest being that it can't be completed without some hex editing to get past a door very near the end of the game, the door is impossible to get through without editing your way past it.

The next drawback is there is no ingame map, and seeing as everywhere looks pretty much the same you can be wandering around for many real life hours trying to find a particular place ... Next, camping in the outside game map is particulary hard as you are constantly woken up to fight yet another horde of bad guys, fatigue quickly sets in so you have to keep reloading a save in the hope that the game gives you a break and lets you sleep so that you can move on.

The above is the worst parts of the game, in general it is fun earning money "Through  Fighting Mainly" to get better armour and equipment, and the inventory management is endless though satisfying.

Botton line is you need to fight "A Lot" to make money to buy things like armour weapons and food ... Check your "Charactor Screen" after EVERY fight and save after every fight and even every action like before fights in Cities ... It is very randon and it's easy to get wiped out in a fight!

Daemongate is old school, the fights are brutal ... Main thing to remember is check your fatigue after every fight and if it's a couple of points down eat some food and save, fatigue is your enemy if an an enemy flees on the battlefield, it will drain you very quickly ... You can control how many bad guys you want to fight if you are aware of exactly when a fight is going to happen by saving just before the battle and loading again if you are not happy with the number of enemys, it's pointless fighting one enemy as there is no profit in it, keep loading until you get  a larger number.

Always keep your armour to "Good" condition as just one piece that is in "Bad" or "Terrible" condition will get that party member killed!

The way to win is throught rigid and O.C.D inventory management.

Still playing it now, though i can't remember how to do the hex editing, though i.m sure i will work it out

There is a walkthrough on the net, you can't miss it, it's the only one ... Follow it to the letter, as the game is event driven, as in B won't happen before you do A.
